findings.title: Validator mutates DB state (match_count) during validation
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves the record on every call. The validator runs on every `valid?` or `save`, so a single signup attempt (the controller calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`) counts twice. Any validation, including `change_username` or other flows that call `valid?` on a changed email, also bumps the stats. The counts are inflated, and a validation step now writes to the database, which is a side effect inside validation.

findings.title: Case-sensitive email lookup lets blocked emails bypass the check
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact, case-sensitive match. A blocked address such as `bad@spam.com` can be bypassed by registering as `Bad@Spam.com`. The email is neither normalized nor downcased on save or on lookup, although the rest of the app uses `Email.downcase`.

findings.title: Non-atomic counter update
findings.body: `match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a read-modify-write. Concurrent signups can lose increments. Use `update_all` with `match_count = match_count + 1`, or `increment_counter`, instead.

findings.title: Validator can raise on nil email
findings.body: `validates :email, email: true` runs when the email changed, including a change to nil. `email_in_restriction_setting?` then runs `nil =~ regexp`, which is fine, but `BlockedEmail.should_block?(nil)` runs an unnecessary query. Skipping blank values would avoid this.
